--- FILE: .plaesy/spec/checkout-payment/spec.md ---
# Spec: Checkout Page with Card and Bank Transfer Payments

Status: draft
Topic: checkout-payment

## Purpose

This spec defines quality requirements for a checkout page that accepts two payment methods: credit/debit card and bank transfer. The page must validate payment information, switch between payment methods, handle errors gracefully, and confirm successful payment initiation. Testing covers payment entry, validation, method switching, error states, and successful submission.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criterion (Given / When / Then) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Display card payment fields | Given the checkout page loads, when the card payment method is selected, then card number, expiry, and CVV input fields are visible and focused | open |
| R2 | Card number validation | Given a card field is focused, when a user enters an invalid card number format, then an error message "Invalid card number" appears and form submission is disabled | open |
| R3 | Expiry date validation | Given an expiry field is focused, when a user enters an invalid or expired date, then an error message appears and form submission is disabled | open |
| R4 | CVV validation | Given a CVV field is focused, when a user enters fewer than 3 digits, then an error message appears and form submission is disabled | open |
| R5 | Cardholder name field | Given the card payment method is selected, when a cardholder name field is empty and the form is submitted, then an error message "Name required" appears | open |
| R6 | Display bank transfer fields | Given the checkout page loads, when the bank transfer payment method is selected, then account number, bank code, and account holder name fields are visible | open |
| R7 | Bank account validation | Given a bank account field is focused, when a user enters an invalid account number format, then an error message "Invalid account number" appears and form submission is disabled | open |
| R8 | Bank code validation | Given a bank code field is focused, when a user enters an invalid bank code, then an error message "Invalid bank code" appears and form submission is disabled | open |
| R9 | Switch between payment methods | Given card details are partially entered, when the user selects bank transfer method, then the card fields are cleared and bank fields appear without form submission | open |
| R10 | Switch back to card | Given bank transfer details are entered, when the user selects card payment method, then bank fields are cleared and card fields appear | open |
| R11 | Submit valid card payment | Given all card fields are filled with valid data, when the user clicks the submit button, then the form is submitted with a POST request containing encrypted card data | open |
| R12 | Submit valid bank transfer | Given all bank transfer fields are filled with valid data, when the user clicks the submit button, then the form is submitted with a POST request containing bank details | open |
| R13 | Disable submit button on invalid form | Given any required field is empty or contains invalid data, when the user views the submit button, then the button is disabled and unclickable | open |
| R14 | Enable submit button on valid form | Given all required fields are filled with valid data, when the user completes the last field, then the submit button becomes enabled and clickable | open |
| R15 | Display loading state during submission | Given a valid form is submitted, when the request is processing, then a loading indicator appears and the submit button is disabled with a "Processing" label | open |
| R16 | Show success message | Given a payment request succeeds, when the response is received, then a success message appears and the user is redirected to the order confirmation page | open |
| R17 | Display error message on failure | Given a payment submission fails, when the error response is received, then an error message is displayed describing the reason (e.g., "Card declined", "Invalid account") | open |
| R18 | Recover from submission error | Given a payment submission failed, when the user corrects the payment details and resubmits, then the form clears the previous error message and processes the new request | open |
| R19 | Prevent duplicate submissions | Given a form is submitted, when the submit button is clicked multiple times rapidly, then only one payment request is sent | open |
| R20 | Display required field indicators | Given the checkout page loads, when the user views the form, then all required fields are marked with a red asterisk or "required" label | open |

## Non-goals

- Testing payment processing backend logic or transaction settlement
- Testing currency conversion or multi-currency support
- Testing 3D Secure or advanced fraud detection flows
- Testing saved payment method features or payment history
- Performance testing or load testing
- Accessibility compliance testing (WCAG standards)
- Mobile responsiveness (separate from desktop checkout flow)

## Open questions

- UNKNOWN: What card types are supported (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, etc.)? Should the form validate against specific card types? Owner: Product.
- UNKNOWN: What bank transfer systems are supported (ACH, Wire, SEPA, Local)? Owner: Product.
- UNKNOWN: Are there geographic restrictions on payment methods (card vs. bank transfer by region)? Owner: Product/Compliance.
- ASSUMED — Form validation occurs client-side before submission: Confirm whether server-side validation also occurs and whether client validation must match server rules.
- ASSUMED — Card data is not stored or logged: Confirm PCI DSS compliance approach (e.g., tokenization, third-party processor).
- ASSUMED — Expiry format is MM/YY: Confirm expected format for test data entry.
- ASSUMED — All error messages are user-friendly English text: Confirm localization requirements.
- UNKNOWN: What is the expected success response time? Should there be a timeout threshold? Owner: Backend/Infrastructure.
- UNKNOWN: Are there rate limits or cooldown periods between submission attempts? Owner: Backend.

## Environments and test data

**Test environments:**
- Staging: Against sandbox payment processor API
- Local/dev: With mocked payment API responses (for offline testing)

**Test data sets:**
- Valid card: 4111111111111111 (Visa test card)
- Valid expiry: 12/25
- Valid CVV: 123
- Valid cardholder name: Test User
- Valid bank account: 123456789 (format varies by region — ASSUMED)
- Valid bank code: TESTBANK
- Valid account holder name: Test User
- Invalid card: 1234567890123456
- Invalid expiry: 01/20 (expired)
- Invalid CVV: 12
- Expired card: 01/23

## Non-functional checks

- **Security**: Card and bank details are transmitted over HTTPS; sensitive data is not logged or exposed in browser console
- **Accessibility**: Form labels are associated with inputs; error messages are announced to screen readers (ASSUMED — confirm requirement)
- **Browser compatibility**: Form works on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (current versions)
- **Performance**: Form loads in under 2 seconds; validation response is immediate (< 100ms)

## Exit criteria

All requirements (R1–R20) have passed acceptance testing in the staging environment with both card and bank transfer payment flows. No critical or high-priority bugs remain open. Error message text and UI layout match the approved design spec. Payment submission does not create duplicate transactions under rapid-click scenarios.

## References

None at this time. Payment method support, compliance requirements, and processor APIs should be documented separately.
